_comment: Article IV kill-fixture for the privacy gate (pipeline/privacy.py). Every string here is a REAL
phrase measured in the OnScript corpus that a careless suppression form would delete. load()
asserts that no admitted form matches any of them, and the assertion runs on every import — so a
future session cannot widen the list into an asymmetric instrument without the run dying.
This file names no private individual. It exists to protect legitimate speech, not to hide it.
'sebastian' is the worked example: it has 37 legitimate uses across the 25-year archive (Sebastian
Gorka, a public official; and the Arkansas county delegation), so admitting it would delete R-side
county-delegation phrases in order to protect a D-side victim. It is REJECTED for that reason.
